## Natural history notes

A small owlet moth characterized by mottled gray to brown forewings with three distinct pale or dark spots, giving it the “three-spot” appearance, and a bark-like pattern that helps it blend against trunks and dead leaves. In Florida, Harris’s Three-Spot is found in wooded and semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, forest edges, pine-oak woods, parks, and shaded yards where suitable hardwood host plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on tree and shrub foliage and contribute to the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
